curation.notes: Open-hardware instrument paper: a low-cost (~€9) glass microfluidic flow cell with a piezo actuator that acoustically traps 1.5 μm polystyrene beads (7.5 MHz, 23.7 Vpp) at ~50 μm depth in a 100 μm channel. Only bead trapping/calibration is shown; tethered-DNA force spectroscopy is stated as future intent, so no biomolecular construct is measured.

trap_stiffness.note: acoustic trap stiffness, reported as approximately 0.6 pN/μm

evidence.snippet: The trap located at 50 ± 0.1 μm depth was measured to have a stiffness of approximately 0.6 pN/μm.
Beads with 1.5 μm diameter flowing in a 100 μm deep channel were trapped at 7.5 MHz using a 23.7 peak-to-peak voltage (Vpp) sinusoidal input.
